call_memory.statement: Thyrocare expects steady-state gross margins for the business to be around 73% to 74% in FY27.

penalties.details: The Chief Judicial Magistrate, Varanasi, has issued a summons citing violations under the Uttar Pradesh Shops and Establishments Act ("the Act"), in connection with an inspection conducted and a notice issued by the Labour Office in September 2023 for non-compliances including non-presentation of registration of Company under the Act during inspection, lack of intimation to labour department for change in details of employees, non-closure of lab during weekly holiday as per Act, non-closure of lab during scheduled holidays as per the Act, deductions in wages apart from what is allowed as per the Act, etc. The summons alleges non-compliance with the provisions of the said Act. Mr. Rahul Franklin Guha, CEO & Managing Director of the Company has been directed to pay a total penalty of ₹6,000 in respect of such non-compliance.
penalties.impact: The penalty amount of ₹6,000 has been paid. There is no material impact on the financials, operations, or other activities of the Company.

timeline.summary: Thyrocare Technologies Limited cancels its earnings conference call for Q4FY26 and FY26 results on May 7, 2026, due to unforeseen circumstances.
Thyrocare Technologies reported Q4FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹223.95 Cr and PAT of ₹48.70 Cr.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹223.95 Cr (+19.7% YoY), net profit to shareholders ₹47.12 Cr (+117.1% YoY).
Thyrocare Technologies Limited’s Board recommended a final dividend of ₹7 per equity share for FY2025-26, subject to AGM approval.
Thyrocare Technologies approved a ₹5.5 Cr investment in its subsidiary Think Health, recommended a final dividend of ₹7 per share, and appointed Price Waterhouse as statutory auditors.
Thyrocare Technologies Limited shared the audio recording of its May 12, 2026, post-results earnings conference call on its website.
Thyrocare Technologies reported Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹224 Cr and PAT of ₹48.7 Cr, driven by strong test volume growth.
Docon Technologies Private Limited, as Promoter, declared no new encumbrances on Thyrocare Technologies Limited’s shares (60.93% pledged) for FY2025-26, excluding prior disclosures.
Promoter Docon Technologies partially redeemed Series 1 NCDs, reducing outstanding principal to ₹1,050 Cr with encumbered shares unchanged at 60.92%.
Thyrocare held its Q1FY27 earnings call on July 23, 2026, reporting 24% revenue growth and 34% PAT growth, and announced plans to explore divesting its radiology business.
Q2FY27 results (consolidated): revenue ₹270.81 Cr (+25.1% YoY), net profit to shareholders ₹15.89 Cr (-66.9% YoY).

Thyrocare reported Q2FY27 consolidated revenue of ₹270.8 Cr (+25.1% YoY) and PAT before exceptions of ₹60.2 Cr (+25.7% YoY), alongside a ₹45 Cr impairment on the proposed divestment of radiology subsidiary Nueclear Healthcare for ₹141.4 Cr.
Audio recording of earnings conference call held on Thursday, October 29, 2026, is available on the company’s website.
Shareholders passed postal ballot special resolutions approving the purchase of land and building from Nueclear Healthcare and the divestment of the entire stake in Nueclear to Trovera Healthcare.
Thyrocare executed a Share Purchase Agreement to sell its entire 100% stake in subsidiary Nueclear Healthcare to Trovera Healthcare for ₹141.40 Cr.
